title: Route validates a parsed URL but stores the raw string — validated value != stored value
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/watched-sources.ts:31-39 parses via new URL(value); line 70 stores `url: body.url` verbatim. Probe: a value with leading/trailing spaces (" https://ok.com ") and one with a trailing newline are both accepted and stored with the whitespace intact; a value written with backslashes after the scheme (http: slash backslash slash backslash evil.com) is accepted, because WHATWG normalises backslashes to slashes giving host evil.com, and is then stored with the backslashes still in it. A future fetcher using a different URL parser (curl, python-requests, Go net/url) may resolve or reject the stored string differently from the one this route approved.
checker_note:
Verified closed at cycle 1, commit c8da5ee: normalisedHttpUrl() returns parsed.href and the route stores that value (watched-sources.ts:38-46,74). Re-probed - " https://ok.com 
" stores https://ok.com/ and the backslash form http:/\/\evil.com/ stores http://evil.com/, so the raw string no longer reaches the collection. Admission predicate byte-for-byte unchanged, so no new bypass. Stays fixed (not verified) until a later re-check.
verified_note: closed by checker evidence review: qa/verdicts/watched-sources-url-normalisation.md (cycle 1 PASS, commit c8da5ee); verdict names this issue and its recorded reproduction was re-derived by the checker; reviewed SHA is an ancestor of origin/master.

title: No internal-address block anywhere in the Watched Sources pipeline — stored SSRF, owed by the fetcher unit
evidence: Probe against the route's isHttpUrl: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/, http://localhost:27017/, http://127.0.0.1:6379/, http://[::1]:8080/ and http://10.0.0.5/ all pass and are stored. NOT a defect of this unit — a store-time hostname check cannot survive DNS rebinding between registration and fetch, so the sound place is the fetcher, on the resolved IP after DNS. Filed against the unbuilt fetcher/scheduler unit and recorded as contract invariant [I3] so it cannot fall between two units neither of which owns it.
checker_note: Closed at cycle 2, commit 26e283a, for the half [I3] actually asserts: the network-level defence exists, lives on the resolved addresses after DNS, and now reaches the same verdict in every spelling. The residual check-to-connect window is NOT part of this closure and is carried separately as ISS-C-UNRUN-WRITERS-011. Stays 'fixed' (not 'verified') until a later re-check.

title: mc-precommit.ps1 resolves the armed-mutation ledger against CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, not the worktree being committed to, so ONE lane's live mutation blocks commits in EVERY other lane
evidence: Observed 2026-09-08 in D:\KnowledgeBase-lanes\c-unrun-writers. Committing the guarded-fetcher unit was refused with 'BLOCKED: a mutation is still armed ... apps/api/src/indexing/vector-gap.ts'. That file does not exist in this worktree at all -- it is the OTHER maker loop's in-flight work in the main tree. Cause: .claude/hooks/mc-precommit.ps1:13 does `if ($env:CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR) { Set-Location $env:CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR }` and then reads `qa/.mutations-active` at :21, so every worktree's pre-commit consults D:\KnowledgeBase's ledger. The main tree's ledger currently holds {"path":"apps/api/src/indexing/vector-gap.ts","pid":38932}. The guard's INTENT is right and was earned the hard way (it exists because the ISS-083 score:0.5 mutation was found applied to production source), but its scope is the repo rather than the checkout.
impact: A lane cannot commit while any other lane is mid-mutation-test, which is most of the time under the concurrent-loop model. Worse for safety than for throughput: the natural workaround is to delete another lane's ledger row or bypass the hook, which disarms a live control protecting production source. I did neither -- the commit is being held instead.
fix_direction: Resolve the ledger against the worktree being committed to: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (or $PWD before the Set-Location) rather than CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, so each checkout has its own qa/.mutations-active. Keep the CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR fallback for the non-worktree case. ENFORCEMENT PATH: .claude/hooks/* changes require an authorizing DECISIONS entry carrying 'Approved-by: Umesh' per the project CLAUDE.md, so this is NOT a maker fix -- it needs the Approver. Fourth cross-loop leak today after ISS-100, ISS-102/103 and the divergent-id gate; see qa/gates/ledger-id-divergence.md and qa/gates/concurrent-maker-sessions.md.

title: Range table blocks the dotted spelling of v4-embedding IPv6 prefixes but allows the hex spelling — 6to4, NAT64 and Teredo walk through
evidence: packages/ingest/src/sources/guarded-fetch.ts:74-86. The unwrap at :77-79 reads only the text after the LAST colon, so it fires only when the embedded v4 is written in dotted form. Probed against the shipped isBlockedAddress: '64:ff9b::127.0.0.1' -> BLOCK but '64:ff9b::7f00:1' (same address, NAT64, embeds 127.0.0.1) -> ALLOW; '2002:7f00:0001::1' (6to4, embeds 127.0.0.1) -> ALLOW; '2002:c0a8:0101::1' (6to4, embeds 192.168.1.1) -> ALLOW. 2001::/32 (Teredo) is likewise unlisted. An attacker controls their own AAAA record, so emitting any of these is free, and on a host with 6to4 or a NAT64/DNS64 network these route to the embedded v4 — precisely the ranges blockedIpv4 exists to refuse. The table's own dotted-form block shows the intent; the hex form is the gap.
fix_direction: Parse the v6 address into its 8 groups rather than string-matching a tail. Block 2002::/16, 64:ff9b::/96 and 2001::/32 outright, and for ::ffff:0:0/96, ::/96, 2002::/16 and 64:ff9b::/96 reconstruct the embedded v4 from the group values and run blockedIpv4 on it, so both spellings reach the same verdict. Add a test per prefix in BOTH notations.
checker_note: Verified closed at cycle 2, commit 26e283a. isBlockedAddress now parses into 8 groups (parseIpv6Groups, guarded-fetch.ts:80-119) and judges numbers instead of text. I re-probed every spelling myself: 64:ff9b::7f00:1, 2002:7f00:0001::1, 2002:c0a8:0101::1, ::ffff:7f00:1, 0:0:0:0:0:ffff:7f00:1, 2002:a9fe:a9fe::1 (6to4 to 169.254.169.254), 2002:0a00:0001::1, 2002:: (all-zero 6to4), uppercase forms, bracketed and zone-suffixed forms -> ALL BLOCK; 2002:0808:0808::1 and 64:ff9b::8.8.8.8 correctly ALLOW, so it is not blocking the prefixes wholesale. Teredo 2001::/32 blocks, 2001:db8::1 correctly allows. Mutants: stop unwrapping 6to4 73/2; stop unwrapping NAT64 73/2; delete the ::ffff:0:0/96 unwrap 72/3 (mine, not the maker's). Every range in the table is behind a killing test.

title: Module docstring claims the checked resolution is the one the caller uses; nothing pins it, so the check-to-connect rebinding window is fully open
evidence: packages/ingest/src/sources/guarded-fetch.ts:16-17 states 'lookup and request are injected so ... the resolution the guard checks is the same one the caller will use', and the commit message for 43c1281 repeats it. But the injected seam is `request(url: string)` (:27) and the call site is `deps.request(current.href)` (:123) — request receives a HOSTNAME and performs its own independent resolution. The address isBlockedAddress approved at :119 is never handed to the transport and never pinned. The unit therefore closes the register-to-fetch window (its real and valuable contribution) but leaves the check-to-connect window entirely open, which is the window classic DNS rebinding actually exploits. Verified by reading the seam signature, not inferred.
fix_direction: Either widen the seam to `request(url: string, address: string)` and require the transport to connect to that address with the original Host header (real pinning), or amend the docstring and the next commit message to state plainly that the checked address is not pinned and name the residual window. The claim as written tells a future reader the module has a property it does not have.
checker_note: Verified closed at cycle 2, commit 26e283a. The false sentence is gone; guarded-fetch.ts:17-24 now carries an explicit HONEST LIMIT block naming the check-to-connect window, saying plainly that request re-resolves independently, and stating exactly what the module DOES guarantee (every returned address is checked). My cycle-1 fix direction was deliberately disjunctive - pin the address OR state the window plainly - and the maker took the second branch, which is what I asked for. lookup also widened to Promise<string[]> with all-must-pass and a fail-closed empty answer (:200-208); mutants 'check only the FIRST address' 74/1 and 'allow an empty resolver answer' 74/1 both die. The residual window itself is now tracked as ISS-C-UNRUN-WRITERS-011, so an honest comment cannot become the place a real gap goes to be forgotten.

title: fec0::/10 deprecated IPv6 site-local is allowed by the link-local regex
evidence: packages/ingest/src/sources/guarded-fetch.ts:83 uses /^fe[89ab][0-9a-f]?:/ which matches fe80::/10 only. Probed: isBlockedAddress('fec0::1') -> ALLOW. fec0::/10 is deprecated (RFC 3879) but is still configured on legacy and appliance networks, and a deny-list guard has no reason to admit it.
fix_direction: Widen to /^fe[89a-f]/ or block fe00::/8 wholesale — nothing in fe00::/9 is a legitimate public fetch target either. Add a test.
checker_note: Verified closed at cycle 2, commit 26e283a. guarded-fetch.ts:159 masks with 0xffc0 === 0xfec0, covering fec0::/10 end to end. Probed: fec0::1 and feff::1 (top of the range) both BLOCK; fe80::1 and febf::1 still block; mutant 'allow fec0::/10' dies 74/1.

title: maxBytes is asserted after the whole body is already in memory, is skipped entirely on redirect hops, and there is no request timeout at all
evidence: packages/ingest/src/sources/guarded-fetch.ts:132-134 checks res.body.length AFTER `request` has returned a fully materialised string, so a hostile endpoint has already been allowed to allocate it — the cap documents an intent the code does not enforce. The redirect branch at :125-130 returns before the size check, so redirect bodies are unbounded regardless. The GuardedFetchDeps interface (:22-29) has no timeout field and guardedFetch never races a deadline, so a slow-loris endpoint hangs an unattended timer-driven fetcher indefinitely. This project already has D-020 because an unbounded hang took out the test suite today.
fix_direction: Move the cap into the transport seam (pass maxBytes to `request` and have it abort the stream when exceeded), apply it on every hop, and add a per-request timeout to GuardedFetchDeps enforced with an AbortSignal or Promise.race.
checker_note: STILL OPEN after cycle 2 - one of its three parts was fixed. FIXED: the size cap now runs on every hop before the redirect branch (guarded-fetch.ts:209-211); my mutant 'drop the redirect-hop size check' dies 74/1. NOT FIXED (a): maxBytes is still asserted on res.body.length after 'request' has returned a fully materialised string, so the cap still documents an intent the code does not enforce and a hostile endpoint still gets the allocation. NOT FIXED (c): there is still NO duration bound - grep -niE 'timeout|abort|deadline|signal|setTimeout' over the module returns nothing and GuardedFetchDeps has no timeout field. (c) needs no transport at all: a timeoutMs on the deps plus Promise.race/AbortSignal around deps.request is enforceable at this layer today, so it is an unforced miss rather than a scope boundary. The manifest lists ISS-009 under 'Issues addressed' while its own Known-gaps section admits the timeout is unfixed - the same species of overclaim as ISS-007, in the same unit. Contract [C7] therefore stays FAILED at cycle 2. | CLOSED at cycle 3 (commit 948212e). All three parts now hold, each re-derived by me. (a) maxBytes is handed to the transport: GuardedFetchDeps.request now takes opts {maxBytes,timeoutMs} (guarded-fetch.ts:44-47) and guarded-fetch.ts:232 passes it; my probe observed the fake transport receive {maxBytes:42,timeoutMs:1000}, and the mutant 'pass Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER instead of maxBytes' dies 78/1. (b) the per-hop size check survives (:240). (c) a TOTAL wall-clock deadline now exists (:205) and each hop is given the REMAINING budget (:225) raced against the transport (:231-236); my redirect probe observed per-hop budgets [300,194,83]ms and the fetch aborted at 307ms rather than after N*timeout, and the mutant 'renew the budget every hop' dies 77/2 while the mutant 'delete the race entirely' dies with the run exiting 1 in 7s. What remains is NOT part of -009: the race cannot cancel the loser (filed separately as ISS-C-UNRUN-WRITERS-015, blocking on the transport unit).

title: The check-to-connect window is honestly stated but still open: request takes a URL and re-resolves, so no approved address is ever pinned to a connection
evidence: packages/ingest/src/sources/guarded-fetch.ts:39 declares request(url: string) and :212 calls deps.request(current.href); the addresses approved at :210 are never handed to the transport. Split out of ISS-C-UNRUN-WRITERS-007 at cycle 2: -007 was a DOCSTRING overclaim and is genuinely fixed, but the underlying window it papered over is not, and closing an issue whose text was about honesty must not silently close the gap that honesty describes. Ruled at cycle 2 that STATING it is sufficient for THIS unit - the transport is explicitly out of scope in the contract, and a request(url, pinnedAddress) signature written with no transport behind it would be a guess at the contract the transport needs - but NOT sufficient for the feature.
fix_direction: BLOCKING on the transport unit: the real-transport unit MUST NOT be accepted unless it connects to a pinned, pre-approved address while presenting the original Host header and SNI. This row is the mechanism that makes an honest comment load-bearing instead of forgettable; it is not closeable by editing prose.
checker_note: ESCALATED medium->high at watched-sources-run cycle 1. The transport unit this row was declared BLOCKING on has now arrived (node-transport.ts, commit d12232a) and does NOT pin: httpRequest calls bare fetch(url), so the OS re-resolves independently of the addresses the guard just approved. store.ts:294 composes it and production.ts:87 wires that into the running API, so the check->connect window is no longer theoretical - it is reachable in the production path. Promoted to contract criterion [C7] of qa/contracts/watched-sources-run.md. | CLOSED at watched-sources-run cycle 2 (commit f6f2b86), re-derived by me, not read from the manifest. node-transport.ts now uses node:http/node:https with a custom `lookup` that returns opts.address, and guarded-fetch.ts:232 passes addresses[0]. My own probe (not the maker's test): a URL naming an unresolvable host (nonexistent-host-xyz.invalid:PORT) connected and returned the local server's body -- only possible via the injected address. Fails CLOSED: address '999.999.999.999' against a URL whose hostname DOES resolve rejected with 'Invalid IP address: 999.999.999.999' rather than falling back to real DNS. Mutation 'delete the custom lookup' dies 88/5 against a 93/0 control. Host header preserved (server observed 'pinned.invalid:PORT'). TLS: I built the self-signed HTTPS fixture the maker did not -- with the address pinned to 127.0.0.1 and the URL naming pinned.example, a cert with SAN pinned.example succeeded and a cert with SAN wrong.example was rejected with 'Hostname/IP does not match certificate's altnames', so certificate validation demonstrably binds to the NAME while the address is pinned. One observation, not a defect: when the URL hostname is an IP LITERAL Node skips `lookup` entirely (probe: url 127.0.0.1:PORT with address 127.0.0.2 connected to 127.0.0.1). Harmless here because for a literal the guard's resolveAll returns that same literal, so pinned address == hostname and no window exists.

title: Two parser laxnesses outside the contract's enumerated prefixes: ::ffff:0:0:0/96 v4-translated is allowed, and a malformed :: alongside 8 literal groups parses instead of failing closed
evidence: Probed against the shipped isBlockedAddress at commit 26e283a. (1) '::ffff:0:127.0.0.1' and its hex form '::ffff:0:7f00:1' -> ALLOW. That is RFC 2765's IPv4-translated prefix ::ffff:0:0:0/96 (groups 0,0,0,0,ffff,0,v4hi,v4lo), which the mapped branch at :150 does not match because the 0xffff sits at g[4] rather than g[5]. It is NOT in the contract's [C4] enumeration and I could not demonstrate a live bypass - no mainstream stack kernel-translates it, so a connect leaves as ordinary unreachable IPv6 - hence low, and not a criterion failure. (2) '1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8::' and '::1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8' are malformed (:: must compress at least one group) but reach the fill===0 path at :113-117 and return 8 groups instead of null. I could not construct an under-block from this: the groups returned are the same literal groups written, so the parse is a superset reading and any private prefix still matches; it is also unreachable in practice, since these strings would have to come from a resolver.
fix_direction: Cheap hardening, not a defect: add ::ffff:0:0:0/96 to the unwrap set alongside ::ffff:0:0/96, and reject halves.length===2 when head.length+back.length >= 8. Adding a blocked range is routine under [I1]. A test each if taken.

title: Nothing on disk catches a source commit that ships without its evidence manifest - the ISS-010 failure can recur silently, and did, twice in one unit
evidence: ISS-010's root cause is confirmed (see its checker_note): a PreToolUse deny kills the entire Bash call, so an artifact write bundled ahead of 'git commit' in one command dies with it, and the maker reasonably read the denial as 'the commit was refused'. It then recurred from a bash parse error in a two-heredoc command - different cause, same class: a failed tool call means NOTHING in it happened. (I hit the same class myself writing this ledger update.) .claude/hooks/mc-precommit.ps1:31-35 already enumerates qa/manifests for 'Status: ready-for-check' and WARNs when units await a verdict, but it emits nothing when a commit touches packages/ or apps/ source and no manifest names that unit at all - which is exactly the silent case.
fix_direction: Two parts. (a) Maker discipline, no approval needed, effective immediately: write a manifest as its OWN tool call and confirm it on disk before issuing any command containing 'git commit'; never bundle an artifact write with a commit. (b) Machine backstop: extend mc-precommit.ps1 to WARN when the staged diff touches packages/ or apps/ source and qa/manifests holds no *.md naming that unit. ENFORCEMENT PATH - .claude/hooks/* requires an authorizing DECISIONS entry carrying 'Approved-by: Umesh' per the project CLAUDE.md, so (b) is NOT a maker fix; it needs the Approver, and it can ride along with the ISS-005 decision on the same file rather than opening a second gate.

title: A timeoutMs larger than 2^31-1 collapses the total deadline to ~1ms instead of extending it
evidence: Probed directly against commit 948212e. createGuardedFetcher({timeoutMs: 3_000_000_000}) with a never-settling transport threw 'guarded-fetch: timed out after 3000000000ms' in 5ms, with Node emitting TimeoutOverflowWarning: 3000000000 does not fit into a 32-bit signed integer. Timeout duration was set to 1. Cause: guarded-fetch.ts:234 passes `left` straight to setTimeout, and Node clamps any delay above 2147483647 to 1ms. `left` is derived from timeoutMs (:205,:225), so any budget over ~24.8 days inverts into an instant refusal. Contrast the small end, which is correct: timeoutMs of 0 and of -5000 both throw at :226 before any request is issued (measured 1ms and 0ms) - fail-closed, consistent with [C5].
fix_direction: Cheap hardening, not a defect: clamp the setTimeout delay to 2147483647 (or reject a timeoutMs above it at construction). Not a [C7] failure - the bound still bounds, it merely over-bounds, and it fails closed rather than open. Availability-only, and unreachable for a fetcher nobody configures with a 25-day budget.

title: The deadline bounds the CALLER but cannot cancel the transport: Promise.race leaves the loser running and `request` accepts no AbortSignal
evidence: guarded-fetch.ts:231-236 races deps.request against a timer and clears the timer in .finally(), but nothing cancels deps.request itself, and the opts argument (:46) carries maxBytes and timeoutMs only. Reproduced: a fetcher with timeoutMs 50 and a transport settling at 400ms rejected on schedule, and the abandoned transport still ran to completion afterwards (observed settling 350ms after the caller had already given up). With the current injected seam this leaks only a promise; with a real socket-backed transport that ignores its own timeoutMs it leaks a live connection per timed-out fetch on an unattended timer, which is the resource-exhaustion shape the deadline was added to prevent. The maker disclosed this itself in the manifest's note to the checker and did not claim otherwise in the module - the docstring's claim is scoped to 'must not be able to hang this caller', which is literally true.
fix_direction: BLOCKING on the transport unit, same mechanism as ISS-C-UNRUN-WRITERS-011: the real-transport unit MUST NOT be accepted unless request accepts an AbortSignal in opts, the fetcher aborts it when the deadline wins, and the transport actually tears down the socket on abort. Ruled at cycle 3 that adding the signal is NOT required of THIS unit - the transport is out of scope in the contract and no caller exists - but unlike the pinned address of ISS-011, `signal: AbortSignal` is a single standard shape (node:https, undici and fetch all take one), so it is the cheapest thing the transport unit will owe and should be written into that contract up front rather than discovered.
checker_note: Fixed in behaviour at watched-sources-run cycle 1, at the layer that owns the socket: httpRequest passes AbortSignal.timeout(opts.timeoutMs) and guarded-fetch.ts:232 hands it the REMAINING total budget (left), so the socket is torn down on the deadline rather than merely abandoned. Measured by checker probe against a local server sleeping 3000ms with timeoutMs 300: rejected with 'The operation was aborted due to timeout' after 308ms. Not moved to verified: the proof is the checker's own probe, not a repo test - no test kills the removal of the signal (see ISS-C-UNRUN-WRITERS-016).

title: All three of the transport's network-facing safety properties survive mutation: no test kills redirect:"manual", the size abort, or the AbortSignal
evidence: Mutation table run against commit d12232a with a no-op control (control: ingest pass 88 fail 0 cancelled 0). Deleting `redirect: "manual"` from node-transport.ts:44 -> pass 88 fail 0. Deleting `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(opts.timeoutMs)` :45 -> pass 88 fail 0. Neutering the size abort at :65 (if (bytes > opts.maxBytes) -> if (false)) -> pass 88 fail 0. node-transport.test.ts exercises resolveAll only; httpRequest has no test at all, so the three properties the module's own docstring calls 'the whole control' are proven exclusively in the guard's fakes. Kills for contrast, same table: due-check removed -> 2 fail; failure isolation removed -> 2 fail; all:true removed -> 1 fail; run-route scope guard removed -> 1 fail.
fix_direction: A local http.createServer fixture, ~40 lines. The checker built one during this check and all three properties passed against real sockets on the first run (302 returned unfollowed with an empty body; a streamed multi-MB body threw 'node-transport: response too large (> 50000 bytes)'; a 3000ms server answered in 308ms under timeoutMs 300). The behaviour is right; only the guard against its regression is missing. Contract [C6] of watched-sources-run.md.
checker_note: CLOSED at watched-sources-run cycle 2. node-transport.test.ts now drives a real http.createServer. I reproduced the whole mutation table myself under D-020 (timeout per run, restore from backup, md5sum -c byte-identical after each, `cancelled` grepped alongside `fail`): control 93/0/0; unpin 88/5/0; size abort neutered 92/1/0; timeout neutered 92/1/0. The three properties that survived at cycle 1 now each kill at least one test. Remaining unpinned line disclosed by the maker and confirmed by me: removing res.destroy() on the redirect path is 93/0/0 -- accepted as resource hygiene rather than a control (the body is never read either way, so no test could honestly cover it); low, noted in the cycle-2 verdict.

title: The feature's SSRF boundary can be replaced with a bare fetch and the whole api suite still passes - the maker's own claim, confirmed
evidence: Replacing apps/api/src/store.ts:294 createGuardedFetcher({ lookup: resolveAll, request: httpRequest }) with async (u: string) => await (await fetch(u)).text() leaves apps/api at pass 134 fail 0 cancelled 0. createMongoWatchedSourceDeps has exactly one caller (production.ts:87) and no test, so every control in guarded-fetch.ts - three fix cycles and six checker rounds of range tables - is one word from being bypassed with nothing on disk objecting. The maker named this in the module comment and in the manifest; the comment is true and is not itself a control.
fix_direction: An assertion the repo already has a precedent for: apps/api's suite contains 'store.ts imports treeIndexRootFilter and both its tree_index call sites use it, not a hand-written copy'. The same source-level assertion over store.ts's run composition, or a structural guard where runWatchedSources refuses a fetcher that did not come from createGuardedFetcher (a brand on the returned function). Contract [C8] of watched-sources-run.md.

title: POST /watched-sources/run's tenant argument is unpinned: swapping req.auth for a literal other tenant passes all 134 api tests
evidence: Mutating routes/watched-sources.ts:99 deps.run(req.auth!.tenantId) to deps.run("other-tenant") -> apps/api pass 134 fail 0 cancelled 0. Cause is in the fake: fixtures.ts:131 defines run: async () => ({ checked: 0, ... }), which takes no argument and therefore cannot observe one - the precise anti-pattern watched-sources-entrypoint.md [I1] names ('a fake backed by one shared array cannot fail an isolation test'). The create and listActive routes ARE pinned by tests; the new third route is not. No live cross-tenant defect: the production path does pass req.auth's tenant through to listActive and recordFetch, both scopedCollection-bound. This is a missing guard, not a present leak.
fix_direction: Make the fake record its tenantId argument and assert the route passes the authenticated one, matching the treatment the other two routes already get. Contract [C9] of watched-sources-run.md.

title: recordFetch's boolean is discarded, so a fetch that persisted nothing is still counted as checked and changed
evidence: packages/db/src/collections/watched-sources.ts:27 returns result.matchedCount > 0 deliberately, and run.ts:59 awaits the call and ignores the value, then increments checked/changed unconditionally at :64-65. Probed directly: a deps set whose recordFetch returns false for two due sources produced {checked:2, changed:2, skipped:0, failed:[]} - a clean success summary for a run that wrote nothing. Self-healing on the happy path (lastFetch unchanged, so the source stays due and is retried), but a source deleted or re-tenanted mid-run reports success forever while never persisting, and the summary the route returns to its caller is false. Silent-failure class: a default-value path where a failure looks like a normal count.
fix_direction: Treat false as a per-source failure ('recordFetch matched no row'), the same shape a throw already gets. Contract [I3] of watched-sources-run.md.

title: The run is an unbounded sequential network loop inside one HTTP request handler - no source cap, no whole-run budget, no concurrency guard
evidence: routes/watched-sources.ts:98 awaits deps.run(...) inline, and run.ts:51 iterates every due source sequentially with the guard's 30s DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS per source (guarded-fetch.ts:59). N due sources therefore hold the request open for up to N*30s with no ceiling on N, and nothing prevents two concurrent POSTs from fetching the same sources twice and racing each other's recordFetch. The maker's gap 3 says the route exists precisely so the chain is testable before a scheduler; that reasoning is sound and this is the cost of it, which is why it is a bounded-run issue rather than a route-design objection.
fix_direction: Any one of: a max-sources-per-run cap, an overall run deadline checked between sources, or 202 + a background run with a per-tenant in-flight lock. Contract [I5] of watched-sources-run.md; worth settling before a scheduler is pointed at this, since a timer plus an unbounded run is how an unattended fetcher becomes an outage.

title: pnpm lint:structure is red on lane/c-unrun-writers: apps/api/src is 31 files against a budget of 30
evidence: At 534af4e with a clean tree: `pnpm lint:structure` exits 1 with `apps/api/src: 31 files (budget 30)`. `git ls-tree --name-only ba8f98d apps/api/src/` = 31 entries, at 534af4e = 32; the added file is apps/api/src/watched-run-deps.test.ts, the ISS-017 fix. Both prior cycles' manifests reported lint:structure green; cycle 3's Evidence block is the first to omit it and the first in which it fails.
fix_direction: Either raise the apps/api/src budget in the structure-lint config with a one-line reason, or fold watched-run-deps.test.ts into an existing apps/api/src test file. A red repo gate blocks every later unit in this lane, so fix it in the next unit that touches apps/api/src, before any new file is added there.
resolution: Fixed in cb54652: composition tests re-homed into routes/watched-sources.test.ts (lint-dirsize OK, 75 dirs); manifest count corrected 98 -> 97.

title: Manifest cycle-3 Evidence over-states the ingest test count as 98; the reproducible figure at the submitted commit is 97

fix_direction: Paste counts from the run at the commit being submitted rather than from an earlier working-tree run. ISS-136 class: a number not reproducible at the submitted commit is itself a finding, even when the substantive result (fail 0, cancelled 0) is correct.
